Protect the vulnerable by cutting admin waste, not lifelines.

The Puppy Protection Act (H.R. 2253) mandates 30 square feet per dog over 35 inches long, temperature controls between 45-85°F, and 30 minutes of daily human socialization. While well-intentioned, this bill exemplifies bureaucratic overreach—layering 1,200+ words of federal micromanagement on dog breeders instead of targeting real issues.

Taxpayers fund 18 months of USDA rulemaking for kennel dimensions while border security gets crumbs. If Washington enforced existing cruelty laws instead of inventing new red tape, maybe we’d stop wasting millions inspecting cage sizes while fentanyl floods through unmanned ports.

Priorities matter.
